## The claim

At least one target gene carries a biallelic candidate set in the read-derived calls.

**Prediction if true.** Enumerating over results.it2_read_alleles gives at least one target gene with two rare heterozygous protein-altering or splice-affecting alleles, or one such allele plus an SV or exon-coverage loss, or one homozygous allele.

**What would refute it.** No target gene yields any biallelic candidate — the read route nominates nothing and its weight in the step-6 fusion is set from that.

## History

| Rev | Status | Confidence | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | proposed | — | — |
| 2 | supported | 0.85 | Supported. results.it2_scored_pairs, built from reads recovered by k-mer bait and called by two callers sharing no code with the vendor's, gives four target genes with a biallelic candidate set of rare protein-altering alleles. One sits in the core tier and is the only gene of 792 with both a truncating and a ClinVar-flagged allele, at 43.71x mean depth and 0.85 bait density, so neither coverage nor reachability qualifies the finding. Confidence is held below the evidence's apparent strength because the annotation is a join to the platform's coding_annotations, which cannot judge an allele the delivered callset never reported: 32 such alleles in core-tier genes are uncounted here, so this is a floor on the biallelic set and not a census of it. |
| 3 | supported | 0.88 | Supported, and the claim does not rest on the newly annotated alleles: four target genes, three of them carrying alleles the delivered callset also reported, already met it before stage 11 ran. Completing the annotation raises the count to ten target genes (three core tier) but those additions are unvalidated calls on a baited alignment, so the count is an upper bound and the confidence is held at 0.88 rather than the heuristic's 0.92. What the claim asserts - that at least one target gene carries a biallelic set of rare protein-altering alleles - is met either way. |
